## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The PR tightens `parse_report` so it accepts only the exact header `REPORT v1` instead of any line that starts with `REPORT `, and it adds two tests for rejected headers. The production change is correct, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers the new branch. However, `test_rejects_legacy_header` never reaches the version check, so it cannot catch the regression it names.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — `test_rejects_legacy_header` produces `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"` because `rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces only the last `v1`, which is in the body. The header stays `REPORT v1`, and the fixture has no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at the END check (`app/report.py:3`) before it reaches the version check (`app/report.py:5`). The comment at line 9 ("Guards the new version check by changing the fixture's version to v0") misdescribes what the test does. — If the version check is removed or loosened, this test still passes, so it gives false confidence that legacy headers are rejected. Only the separate `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` actually protects that behavior.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` uses a complete, well-formed report with a `REPORT v0` header. It would fail under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check, so it does exercise the new exact-match branch.
- The production change is small and leaves the existing END/length validation order unchanged.
